# Notes.ThatVetGuy

> Free academic resources, thoughtfully made for future vets.

A free academic directory primarily for BVSc & AH students. Original summaries: Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. External notes and books retain their source credit; links do not imply authorship or medical review.

Main website: https://thatvetguy.net
Author: https://www.linkedin.com/in/drchiragpatidarconnect
Last source review: 2026-10-14; external HTTP availability has not been verified in the build environment.

---
Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/

## Questions, answered

Are the resources hosted here?

Notes.ThatVetGuy organises links to credited external sources. Availability, downloads and access terms belong to each source.

Where should I start?

Choose your professional year in BVSc Notes & Books, or search for a subject, book or clinical reference.

## Questions, answered

Does this grouping match my university?

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus before planning revision.

Where are the books?

Each year has one shared Books for Year collection. Subject Notes and Books tabs point to the relevant material without repeating the same book directory.

# Objective Resources

Find ICAR AIEEA (PG) previous-year papers, subject-wise objective questions and veterinary objective book listings. These resources help veterinary students plan exam revision using credited external collections.

[ICAR PYQ Question Bank](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/objective/#icar-pyq)[Subject-wise Objective Questions](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/objective/#subject-wise)[Objective Books](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/objective/#books)

## ICAR PYQ Question Bank

Browse previous-year papers for veterinary and animal sciences at their source.

PYQ · Vet Study

A year-wise collection maintained by Vet Study.

Start with the question-bank collections below, then choose the subject you are revising.

## Questions, answered

Where can I find ICAR AIEEA PG previous-year papers?

The ICAR PYQ Question Bank section links to the year-wise Vet Study collection. Select the paper and exam year on that source website.

Are the objective books available to download?

The five named book entries are marked Coming soon because individual book links have not been verified. You can request a specific title or edition.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Tips & Tools for Vet Study

# Tips & Tools for Vet Study

Explore practical AI study guidance, useful free apps and everyday study tools for veterinary students. Use the guides to organise reading, references and presentations while checking veterinary information against trusted sources.

[Use of AI for Vet Study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#ai-guide)[Useful Free Apps](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#free-apps)[Useful Study Tools](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#useful-tools)

## Use of AI for Vet Study

Use AI to help organise your work, while keeping your course materials as the source of truth.

- 

### Start with an outline

Ask for a clear structure for a topic, presentation or revision plan.

- 

### Bring your own sources

Work from your notes and check every fact, reference and citation.

- 

### Keep clinical decisions separate

AI-generated study text is not a substitute for professional clinical guidance.

## Useful Free Apps

A small toolkit for writing, reading and organising references.

Tool · Zotero

### Zotero

Organise sources and build bibliographies.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

[Read Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/)[Report broken link](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/?resource=zotero#report)

Tool · LibreOffice

### LibreOffice

Create documents, spreadsheets and presentations.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

[Read LibreOffice](https://www.libreoffice.org/)[Report broken link](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/?resource=libreoffice#report)

## Useful Study Tools

Useful starting points for working with references and PDF study material.

Tool · Mozilla

### PDF.js

Read PDFs in a browser with Mozilla’s open-source viewer.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

[Read PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/)[Report broken link](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/?resource=pdf-js#report)

## Questions, answered

Can I use AI as a clinical reference?

Use AI to help organise study, not to make clinical decisions. Check veterinary facts, citations and drug information against original professional references.

Are these tools all subscription-free?

The free-app listings describe free tools; access conditions can change. Check the source website for current licensing and availability.

Last checked: 2026-10-14. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Clinical Resources

Find veterinary handbooks, drug and analgesic references, and clinical pathology resources. These links support veterinary study and supervised clinical learning; they do not replace professional judgement or a current prescribing reference.

[Handbooks](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/clinical/#handbooks)[Drug & Analgesic References](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/clinical/#drug-index)[Other Clinical Resources](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/clinical/#other-resources)

Study references support learning; they do not replace clinical judgement. Check the complete source, species and context before using drug information. Access to external sites varies.

## Handbooks

Open a professional reference at its source. These are external reading links, not files hosted here.

Handbook · Merck Veterinary Manual

### Merck Veterinary Manual

Veterinary topics, conditions and professional reference material.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

[Read Merck Veterinary Manual](https://www.merckvetmanual.com/)[Report broken link](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/?resource=merck-veterinary-manual#report)

## Drug & Analgesic References

Read the full pharmacology reference for the species and context you are studying.

Drug · Merck Veterinary Manual

### Veterinary NSAID reference

Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the Merck Veterinary Manual.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

[Read Veterinary NSAID reference](https://www.merckvetmanual.com/pharmacology/inflammation/nonsteroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-in-animals)[Report broken link](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/?resource=veterinary-nsaid-reference#report)

Drug · Merck Veterinary Manual

### Analgesics used in animals

Professional reference information, including meloxicam.

Source last checked: 2026-10-14

Is this a complete veterinary drug index?

No. Drug & Analgesic References currently links to Merck material on NSAIDs and analgesics, rather than individual locally maintained drug monographs.

Where can I study veterinary clinical pathology?

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/About Notes.ThatVetGuy

# About Notes.ThatVetGuy

Notes.ThatVetGuy is a free academic resource directory for BVSc & AH students. It brings together credited study links, original subject outlines and practical tools within the ThatVetGuy ecosystem.

## A useful place to start

Notes.ThatVetGuy brings together veterinary notes, books and study resources by professional year, subject and purpose. Browse notes and books, prepare with objective resources, find a clinical reference or explore a practical study tool.

## How the library works

Current listings link to external libraries and professional references. A listing is not a claim that Notes.ThatVetGuy authored, medically reviewed or hosts that resource. Availability and access terms belong to the source website.

## Help improve the library

Found a broken link, need a resource or want to contribute? Email [contact@thatvetguy.net](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net). Please include the resource name, subject and source if you have one.

## Part of ThatVetGuy

[Main website ↗](https://thatvetguy.net) · [Blog ↗](https://blog.thatvetguy.net)

## Questions, answered

Who writes the original guides?

Original site guides and summaries are by Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. External notes, books and references retain their source credit.

Last checked: 2026-10-14. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Can’t find what you need?

Request a veterinary note, book, PYQ or useful study resource, or report a link that needs attention. Include the subject, year and source so the library can be improved for other veterinary students.

## Tell us what would help

Include the title or topic, your professional year and subject. For a book or PYQ, add the edition or exam year if you know it.

[Email your request ](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net?subject=Resource%20request&body=Resource%20or%20topic%3A%20%0ASubject%20and%20year%3A%20%0AEdition%20or%20exam%20year%3A%20%0ASource%20link%20if%20known%3A%20)

Your email app will open. You can also write directly to [contact@thatvetguy.net](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net). Requests help guide future additions; availability is not guaranteed.

## Contact

Email contact@thatvetguy.net. If your email app does not open, copy this address into your preferred email service.

## Contribute a resource

Send the title, subject and original source to contact@thatvetguy.net.

## Report an Error

Send the page URL and the resource name to contact@thatvetguy.net so the link can be reviewed.

## Questions, answered

How do I report a broken link?

Email contact@thatvetguy.net with the page URL and resource name. The visible email address can be copied if your email application does not open.

Can I contribute a resource?

Send the original source, title and subject to contact@thatvetguy.net. Share material you have permission to contribute.

Last checked: 2026-10-14. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Veterinary Anatomy

Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

1st Year · BVSc & AH

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus.

## Revision topic outline

Use this overview to plan reading alongside your university syllabus; it is not an exhaustive syllabus.

- Osteology and arthrology
- Myology and visceral anatomy
- Neuroanatomy and sense organs
- Histology and embryology

Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

## Notes and books

# Veterinary Physiology

Veterinary Physiology focuses on understanding how healthy animals maintain normal body functions. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

1st Year · BVSc & AH

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus.

## Revision topic outline

Use this overview to plan reading alongside your university syllabus; it is not an exhaustive syllabus.

- Blood and cardiovascular physiology
- Respiratory and renal physiology
- Digestion and metabolism
- Endocrine and reproductive physiology

Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

# Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology

Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology focuses on connecting drug action with species, safety and clinical context. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

3rd Year · BVSc & AH

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus.

## Revision topic outline

Use this overview to plan reading alongside your university syllabus; it is not an exhaustive syllabus.

- General pharmacology and pharmacokinetics
- Systemic pharmacology
- Antimicrobial and antiparasitic agents
- Toxicology and poisoning principles

Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.
